# Phase 4 Integration Brief — UI / HUD / Audio / Screens

Read-only scout report for Happy Dog Runner. All cites are `file:line`. **Key headline finding: `AudioManager` is a mute/unlock/persistence shell only — it owns no sound keys and has no `play()`; audio assets are NOT in the manifest (it's SVG-only); and the pause system + pause button do not exist yet and must be built.**

---

## 1. SPEC_REQUIREMENTS

### HUD elements (spec §6.2, `docs/2d-browser-runner-spec.md:284-296`)
Persistent, minimal, thumb-safe. Proposed positions:

| Element | Position | Content |
|---|---|---|
| **Score** | Top-left | Live numeric (`hud_score` + number) |
| **HP hearts** | Top-center or top-left under score | 3 hearts, filled/empty — distinguishable by **shape+fill, not color alone** (§10.4, art-direction.md:60) |
| **Level progress** | Top, full-width thin bar | `distance / LEVEL_LENGTH`; **progress bar preferred over timer** (visualizes finish approaching) |
| **Pause** | Top-right | Opens pause overlay |
| **Mute** | Top-right (next to pause) | Toggles audio |

The HUD progress-bar art (`ui_progress_bar`) is **frame/track only — inner fill is transparent; code draws the dynamic fill on top** (art-direction.md:58).

### Pause & mute (spec §6.3, `:299-301`)
- **Pause overlay:** dims play; shows **Resume + Mute + (optional) Quit-to-menu**; **game clock AND scrolling freeze.**
- **Mute:** toggles all audio; state **persisted** (localStorage) across scenes/sessions; reflected by icon in **menu, HUD, and pause.**
- **`duration_s` must EXCLUDE paused time** (spec §7.2, `track.ts:33`) — currently `elapsedMs += delta` runs every frame (`GameScene.ts:278`), so pause MUST freeze that accumulation.

### Results screens (spec §6.4, `:303-321`)
Both share a layout; only framing/art differ:

| Element | Victory | Game Over |
|---|---|---|
| Headline | "Ти впорався! 🐕" | "Кліщі тебе наздогнали…" |
| Final score | shown | shown |
| Result art | `dog_victory` | `dog_defeat` |
| **Buy CTA (single)** | promo code + "Купити на tabletki.ua" | same |
| Secondary | Play again | Play again |

CTA (locked): **one** primary CTA → displays copyable **promo code** + button to **tabletki.ua**; on tap fire `click_buy` (`destination`, `promo_code`) **then** navigate to the **UTM-tagged** URL (new tab). **No client-site path in MVP** — tabletki.ua only.

### A11y basics (spec §10.4, `:511-518`)
- Large thumb-friendly tap targets; whole canvas = jump zone.
- Sufficient text/HUD contrast; hearts distinguishable by shape+fill not color alone.
- Mute always reachable.
- Full keyboard play on desktop (spacebar jump).
- No essential info by color alone.

### Analytics fire points — checklist (spec §5.2, `:262-270`; §7.2 `:349-371`)
- [x] **`start_game`** — fires once as Play/run begins. **ALREADY WIRED** in `GameScene.ts:121` (`track('start_game')`). No params.
- [x] **`finish_game`** `{result, score, duration_s}` — Victory/GameOver. **ALREADY WIRED** in `GameScene.ts:429` (`endRun`). Win at finish-line overlap (`:231`, `:294-296`); lose at HP≤0 (`:395`).
- [x] **`click_buy`** `{destination, promo_code}` — results CTA tap. **ALREADY WIRED** in `ResultsScene.ts:89` (`onBuy`), then `window.open(buildBuyUrl(), '_blank')` (`:90`).
- ⚠️ The only **new** analytics concern for Phase 4: ensuring `duration_s` excludes paused time once pause exists (§7.2 + `track.ts:33`). All three events and their param shapes are already implemented in `src/analytics/track.ts` (typed overloads `:57-59`; `FinishGameParams` `:29-34`).

### Screen flow (spec §5.1, `:245-259`)
`Menu → Play` (fires start_game) → `Victory|GameOver` (fires finish_game) → `Buy` (fires click_buy) or `Play again` (→ fresh start_game). Pause/Resume loops within Play. All scene keys exist (`src/scenes/keys.ts:2-8`): Boot/Preload/Menu/Game/Results.

---

## 2. AUDIOMANAGER_API

`AudioManager` (`src/systems/AudioManager.ts`) is an **object literal, not a class** — a thin wrapper over the scene's Phaser `BaseSoundManager`. **Full public API (all 4 methods):**

```ts
isMuted(): boolean                                              // AudioManager.ts:31-33
apply(sound: Phaser.Sound.BaseSoundManager): void               // :36-38 — pushes persisted mute: sound.mute = muted
toggle(sound: Phaser.Sound.BaseSoundManager): boolean           // :41-46 — flip + sound.mute + persist; returns new muted
installAudioUnlock(sound: Phaser.Sound.BaseSoundManager): void  // :60-78 — long-lived window pointerdown/touchend → context.resume() once
```

Internals worth knowing:
- Module-level state: `muted` (`:27`, seeded from localStorage `MUTE_STORAGE_KEY='hdr:muted'`, `gameConfig.ts:66`) and `unlockInstalled` guard (`:28`).
- `readStoredMute()`/`persistMute()` wrap localStorage in try/catch so private mode fails open (`:11-25`).
- `apply()` is called once in **BootScene** (`BootScene.ts:17`); `installAudioUnlock()` right after (`:20`).
- The unlock attaches to **`window` pointerdown + touchend** (NOT scene input) precisely because PreloadScene's input shuts down on hand-off (`AudioManager.ts:51-57`); it resumes the suspended WebAudio context then removes itself. Idempotent.

### Verdict: PRELOADED audio keys (not runtime buffers)
- It is built around **Phaser preloaded keys** — playback goes through the scene's `sound` manager (`this.sound.play(key)`), and mute is enforced by setting `sound.mute`. It expects sounds to have been registered via `Phaser.load.audio(...)` in a scene's `preload`.
- It does **NOT** own/register/track any sound keys, has **no `play()` / `add()` / key map**, and stores **no volume config**.
- It does **NOT** synthesize runtime Web Audio buffers/oscillators. **However**, it already reaches the underlying `WebAudioSoundManager.context` (`AudioManager.ts:66-69`) to resume it — so a synthesized-tone path is *physically reachable* via `sound.context`, but that is not the intended design. The clean, idiomatic path is **preloaded keys + `this.sound.play(key, { volume })`**.
- **How to play a sound (recommended):** directly `this.sound.play('sfx_jump')` (Phaser honors the `sound.mute` flag the AudioManager already syncs). Optionally add a tiny `AudioManager.play(sound, key, opts)` helper later, but it is not required — every sound manager already respects the shared mute.
- **iOS unlock requirement (spec §10.2):** handled — call already lives in BootScene. The only open item is the AudioManager's own `TODO(phase-5)` (`AudioManager.ts:58`): verify on real iOS Safari that a muted player who taps Play stays muted through unlock (mute is module state, unaffected by resume, so it should hold).

### ⚠️ Audio assets are NOT loadable today — seam to flag
- `ASSET_MANIFEST` (`assetManifest.ts:41-87`) is **SVG-only**; `AssetDef.type` is the literal `'svg'` (`assetManifest.ts:19`), and `PreloadScene.preload()` loops `load.svg` for every entry (`PreloadScene.ts:29-31`). There is **no audio loading anywhere** (grep for `load.audio` returns nothing).
- **You cannot simply append audio to the existing manifest** without widening `AssetDef.type` and the `gen-placeholders` contract. Recommendation: add a **separate audio key map** (e.g. a small `AUDIO_KEYS` set) + dedicated `this.load.audio(key, [url])` calls in `PreloadScene.preload()` (after the SVG loop). Per spec §8.4, use compressed `.m4a`/`.mp3` + `.ogg` fallback. The 7 required assets (spec §4.6, `:226-235`): jump SFX, hit SFX, pickup SFX, victory sting, game-over sting, music loop, + mute state (code).

---

## 3. GAMESCENE_HOOKS

### GameEvents map (exported, `GameScene.ts:41-48`)
Subscribe on `scene.events` from a future `Hud.ts` / audio wiring. Payloads are primitives:

| Export name | Event string | Payload | Emit site |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GameEvents.runStart` | `'run:start'` | — | `GameScene.ts:122` (once, in `create`) |
| `GameEvents.hp` | `'hud:hp'` | `hp: number` | `:339` (only on change) |
| `GameEvents.score` | `'hud:score'` | `score: number` | `:323` (only on change) |
| `GameEvents.progress` | `'hud:progress'` | `progress: number` (0..1) | `:330` (**every frame**) |
| `GameEvents.armor` | `'hud:armor'` | `{ active: boolean, remainingMs: number }` | `:347` (only on change) |
| `GameEvents.runEnd` | `'run:end'` | `FinishGameParams` `{result, score, duration_s}` | `:430` (in `endRun`) |

Note: `progress` fires every frame; the others are change-gated (`lastHp`/`lastScore`/`lastArmorActive`, `:96-99`). A HUD can subscribe to these instead of polling. The **public read getters** are also available (`liveHp :128`, `liveScore :131`, `liveProgress :134`) if polling is preferred.

### Readout to REMOVE (throwaway in-scene HUD)
The **entire `buildHud()` method**, `GameScene.ts:234-263`:
- progress bar: `ui_progress_bar` image (`:239`) + `progressFill` rectangle (`:240-244`, fill `0x6cc04a`, scaleX tracks progress).
- score row: `ui_score_icon` image (`:248`) + `scoreText` (`:249-257`).
- hearts: `heartImages[]` (`:260-262`, 3× `ui_heart_full`, spaced `44px` from x=42 at y=100).

Coupled state/logic to also remove/redirect to the new Hud:
- Fields `heartImages` (`:84`), `scoreText` (`:85`), `progressFill` (`:86`).
- `refreshHearts()` (`:334-341`) — keeps the `hud:hp` emit; drop the texture swap or move it to Hud.
- `updateHud()` (`:328-332`) — drops `progressFill.scaleX = progress`; keep the `hud:progress` emit.
- `updateScore()` (`:318-326`) — drops `scoreText.setText(...)`; keep the `hud:score` emit.
- `buildHud()` call in `create()` (`:117`); `this.heartImages = []` in `cleanup()` (`:442`).
- The new `Hud.ts` should sit in `src/ui/` (spec §8.2 `:427-429` lists `Hud.ts` + `PauseOverlay.ts` there).

### Whole-canvas jump handler to GATE (`buildInput()`, `GameScene.ts:265-271`)
```ts
this.input.on(Phaser.Input.Events.POINTER_DOWN, () => this.hero.jump());   // :267
this.input.keyboard?.addKey(SPACE).on('down', () => this.hero.jump());     // :269-270
```
Spec §3.2/§10.4: the whole canvas is the jump zone. Two new constraints Phase 4 must enforce:

1. **Taps on pause/mute UI must NOT jump.** Phaser's scene-level `POINTER_DOWN` fires even when an interactive GameObject (button) also receives the event, so it does **not** auto-exclude buttons.
2. **Taps while paused must NOT jump** (and the loop is frozen anyway).

**Recommended gating approach** — replace the `:267` handler with a guarded one:
```ts
this.input.on(Phaser.Input.Events.POINTER_DOWN, (pointer: Phaser.Input.Pointer) => {
  if (this.paused) return;                                   // (2) ignore while paused
  const hit = this.input.hitTestPointer(pointer);            // interactive objs under pointer
  if (hit.length > 0) return;                                // (1) a HUD button (pause/mute) ate it
  this.hero.jump();
});
```
- `hitTestPointer` returns the interactive GameObjects under the pointer — if any pause/mute button has `setInteractive`, its hit-area is reported and the tap is treated as a UI tap, not a jump.
- **No need to re-check airborne/grounded:** `HeroDog.jump()` (`HeroDog.ts:110-111`) already self-guards — *"fires only when grounded & alive; ignored airborne."* (Landing returns to run, `HeroDog.ts:186-189`.)
- A `paused` flag does not yet exist (grep: no `this.scene.pause`/`physics.pause`/`isPaused` anywhere). See Pause note below.

### Pause — does not exist yet (separate from jump gating, but coupled)
Grep found **zero** pause usage in the codebase. Two viable patterns:
- **In-scene overlay + `paused` flag:** set `this.paused = true`; short-circuit `update()` at the top (`:275` currently `if (this.finished) return;` → add `|| this.paused`). This freezes scrolling, spawning, scoring, **and** the `elapsedMs += delta` at `:278` (which is what makes `duration_s` exclude paused time — spec §7.2). Render the `ui_pause_panel` + Resume/Mute/Quit as interactive GameObjects above the HUD. Pause/resume should also stop/resume the music loop.
- **Separate `PauseScene`:** `this.scene.pause(SceneKey.Game)` + `this.scene.launch(SceneKey.Pause)`; pause-by-scene also halts `update()` and thus `elapsedMs`. Requires adding a `Pause` key to `src/scenes/keys.ts:2-8`.

Either works; the in-scene flag is less machinery and keeps the `paused` guard the jump handler needs.

---

## 4. SCENES

### MenuScene (`src/scenes/MenuScene.ts`) — mostly built; polish only
Already present: `document.title = t('menu_title')` (`:24`); full-screen `screen_bg_menu` (`:26`); `ui_title_logo` at y=180 (`:27`); subtitle at y=330 (`:30`); **Play button** via `createButton` at y=450 → `scene.start(SceneKey.Game)` (`:37-43`); hint at y=550 (`:45`); **mute toggle** top-right (`buildMuteToggle :56-74`, `ui_btn_mute_on/off`, refreshes texture+label on toggle). Fires **no** analytics (start_game fires in GameScene). No depth set on menu objects (single-screen, no layering needed).

**Rotate-hint overlay — NOT in MenuScene.** It is a **DOM overlay** mounted once at app boot: `installOrientationGuard()` is called in **`src/main.ts:14`** and defined in `src/ui/OrientationOverlay.ts:9-58`. It builds a `<div id="orientation-guard">` (`role="alertdialog"`, `aria-live="polite"`), shown via `window.matchMedia('(orientation: portrait)')` (`OrientationOverlay.ts:47`) — the `update()` (`:48-50`) sets `display = portrait.matches ? 'flex' : 'none'`, re-evaluated on `change`/`resize`/`orientationchange` (`:52-56`). It lives in the DOM (not a scene) so it covers **all** scenes. **Phase 4 branding/restyle of it is allowed** (the file says "Phase 2 may brand/restyle it," `:7`). Uses `t('rotate_title')`/`t('rotate_body')` (`:19,21`).

### ResultsScene (`src/scenes/ResultsScene.ts`) — fully built; polish only
- Constructor key `Results` (`:17`); `create(data: Partial<FinishGameParams>)` (`:20`) — **robust to missing/partial data** (deep-link/hot-reload safe): defaults to **lose + score 0** (`:23-24`).
- Layout: bg (`screen_bg_victory`/`screen_bg_gameover`, `:27`); `dog_victory`/`dog_defeat` at y=250 (`:28`); title y=90 (`:31`); score `t('results_score',{score})` y=380 (`:40`); promo chip `ui_promo_chip` + code y=460 (`:48-56`); **CTA** `ui_btn_cta` y=565 → `onBuy()` (`:59-65`); **Play again** `ui_btn_play_again` y=660 → `scene.start(SceneKey.Game)` (`:68-74`); **Menu** text link top-left → `scene.start(SceneKey.Menu)` (`:77-85`).
- `onBuy()` (`:88-91`): `track('click_buy', { destination: buyDestination(), promo_code: ENV.promoCode })` then `window.open(buildBuyUrl(), '_blank', 'noopener')`.
- Reusable `createButton` (`src/ui/Button.ts:31`) backs Play/CTA/Play-again — it's a Container with SVG bg + centered label, interactive hit-rect, hover/press scale feedback. **Reuse it for HUD pause/mute and pause-overlay buttons.** (Its label default style is cream text `#f4f7fa` `Button.ts:24-29`.)

---

## 8. GAMECONFIG_TUNING (`src/config/gameConfig.ts`)

- **Hazard spacing** (`:56-57`): `HAZARD_SPACING_START = 640` (within 520–700), `HAZARD_SPACING_END = 360` (within 300–420). Eases generous→tight over the run.
- **Collectible hover** (`:103-104`): `COLLECTIBLE_HOVER_PX = 150` above `GROUND_TOP_Y` (must-jump to collect), `COLLECTIBLE_HOVER_JITTER_PX = 46` (0..N extra upward). `TABLET_SPACING_START = 560` (`:106`).
- **Hero physics body** (`:87-88`): `HERO_BODY_WIDTH = 74`, `HERO_BODY_HEIGHT = 116` (forgiving hitbox, centered on the 140-wide frame, anchored to feet).
- **Parallax factors** (relative to world speed; `:81-84`): `PARALLAX_FACTOR_FAR = 0.16`, `PARALLAX_FACTOR_NEAR = 0.42`, `PARALLAX_FACTOR_GROUND = 1.0`, `PARALLAX_FACTOR_GRASS = 1.12` (far<ground<grass for depth). Applied in `scrollParallax()` (`GameScene.ts:299-304`).
- **Audio-adjacent timing** (for syncing SFX/stings): `HIT_SHAKE_MS = 180` (`:119`), `HIT_FLASH_MS = 120` (`:121`), `ARMOR_EXPIRY_TELL_MS = 1000` (`:115`), `RESULTS_HANDOFF_DELAY_MS = 850` (`:134` — the gap between `runEnd` and the ResultsScene hand-off where a win/lose sting should play; `endRun` schedules it at `GameScene.ts:433`).
- Other relevant: `MAX_HP = 3` (`:21`, heart count), `LEVEL_LENGTH = 40000` (`:40`, progress denominator), `GAME_WIDTH/HEIGHT = 1280/720` (`:14-15`).

No magic numbers in scene code — all tuning is here.

## 9. DEPTH (bands)

Depth is a **scene-private const in GameScene only** — `GameScene.ts:51-60`, **not exported, not in config, not shared**:

```
bgFar: 0, bgNear: 1, ground: 2, grass: 3, entity: 5, hero: 6, aura: 7, hud: 100
```

- **`Depth.hud = 100` confirmed** (`:59`) — all throwaway HUD objects use it (`:239, :243, :248, :257, :261`).
- **No `pause` band exists.** A pause overlay must render **above** the HUD → recommend a new band `pause: 200` (or `overlay`) and a dim/backdrop at ≥150. If the new `Hud.ts` + `PauseOverlay.ts` live in `src/ui/` and are used by GameScene, consider **lifting `Depth` into `src/config/`** so HUD, overlay, and any future scene agree — but minimal change is to just add `pause` to the local const and have the overlay set depth 200.

1	# Game Specification — 2D Browser Runner (Working title: *Happy Dog Runner*)
2	
3	**Document type:** Product & technical specification (buildable scope for estimate)
4	**Status:** Draft for client confirmation
5	**Source of requirements:** [`docs/2d-browser-runner-bi-brief.md`](./2d-browser-runner-bi-brief.md) (client cost-estimation brief, English translation)
6	**Date:** 2026-07-23
7	
8	> **How to read this document.** The client brief is the source of *requirements*. A product interview then locked a set of *decisions* that resolve the brief's open ambiguities (e.g. endless vs. finite, MVP vs. phase 2). Where a locked decision narrows or overrides the brief, this spec follows the decision and says so. Section 11 lists what still needs client confirmation before a firm cost/timeline can be committed.
9	
10	---
11	
12	## 1. Overview & Goals
13	
14	### 1.1 What we are building
15	
16	A **mobile-first, branded 2D browser runner** that promotes a dog flea-and-tick tablet. The player controls a hero dog that auto-runs through a park, jumps over obstacles, avoids **ticks**, and collects **tablets**. The round is a **finite single level (~60–90 s)** ending in **Victory** (reach the finish line) or **Game Over** (lose all health). After the round, a single call-to-action surfaces a **promo code** and links to **[tabletki.ua](http://tabletki.ua)** to buy the product.
17	
18	This is an advergame: the gameplay is the vehicle, and the marketing outcomes are the point.
19	
20	### 1.2 Marketing objective
21	
22	Per the brief (§1), two goals:
23	
24	1. **Awareness** — teach, through play, that ticks are a threat and the tablet is the protection. The "tablet as armor" power-up (§3.7) makes the product mechanic *be* the protection.
25	2. **Conversion** — drive tablet purchase via the post-round CTA to tabletki.ua (brief §3, "CTA button").
26	
27	### 1.3 Audience
28	
29	Dog owners on **mobile web**, reached through paid social / display where Meta Pixel and GA4 attribution matter. Casual players; sessions are short and one-handed. UI language assumed **Ukrainian primary**, built i18n-ready (see §11).
30	
31	### 1.4 Success signals (tied to the three analytics events)
32	
33	The entire funnel is observable through three events (full contract in §7):
34	
35	| Funnel stage | Signal | Event |
36	|---|---|---|
37	| Engagement | Player starts a round | `start_game` |
38	| Completion & quality | Player finishes (win or lose), with score & duration | `finish_game` (`result`, `score`, `duration_s`) |
39	| **Conversion** | Player taps the buy CTA | `click_buy` (`destination`, `promo_code`) |
40	
41	Primary KPI is `click_buy / start_game` (intent-to-purchase rate). `finish_game` with `result=win` vs. `lose` and `duration_s` tells us whether difficulty is tuned so players actually reach the CTA.
42	
43	---
44	
45	## 2. Platforms & Performance Targets
46	
47	### 2.1 Platform priority
48	
49	**Mobile web first**, desktop supported (brief §2). Touch is the primary input; desktop uses tap/click and spacebar.
50	
51	### 2.2 Supported browser matrix
52	
53	| Tier | Browser / OS | Support level |
54	|---|---|---|
55	| Primary | iOS Safari (last 2 major versions) | Fully supported, primary QA target |
56	| Primary | Android Chrome (last 2 major versions) | Fully supported, primary QA target |
57	| Secondary | Desktop Chrome / Edge / Firefox (current) | Fully supported |
58	| Secondary | Desktop Safari (current) | Fully supported |
59	| Best-effort | Samsung Internet, mobile Firefox | Should work; not a QA gate |
60	
61	### 2.3 Performance budget (assumed — **flag for confirmation**, see §11)
62	
63	Because the brief sets no numbers, we propose these targets. They drive art budgets and QA gates and must be confirmed:
64	
65	| Metric | Target | Notes |
66	|---|---|---|
67	| Frame rate | 60 FPS on mid-range phones; **≥30 FPS floor** on low-end (≈2–3-year-old Android) | Gameplay must never dip below the floor |
68	| Time-to-interactive (first load, warm CDN) | **≤3 s** on a 4G connection | Menu interactive |
69	| Initial download (gzipped) | **≤4–6 MB** total (code + assets) | Aggressive for an advergame; see §10.5 |
70	| Input latency (tap → jump) | ≤1 frame of processing | Tap responsiveness is the whole game |
71	| Orientation | Portrait-first; graceful landscape | Confirm preferred orientation |
72	
73	These are the recommended KPIs to lock in §11.
74	
75	---
76	
77	## 3. Gameplay Design
78	
79	### 3.1 Core loop
80	
81	```
82	auto-run forward  →  read upcoming hazard  →  tap to jump  →  land / collect / take hit
83	      ↑                                                                    │
84	      └──────────────────── repeat until finish line or 0 HP ──────────────┘
85	```
86	
87	The player does exactly one thing — **time jumps** — against a scrolling stream of obstacles, ticks, and tablets. Skill = timing and reading density as speed ramps.
88	
89	### 3.2 Controls (locked)
90	
91	**Auto-run + tap-to-jump ONLY.** No duck/slide, no lane-switching in MVP.
92	
93	| Input | Platform | Action |
94	|---|---|---|
95	| Tap anywhere on canvas | Mobile | Jump |
96	| Spacebar / click | Desktop | Jump |
97	| Pause button (HUD) | All | Pause / resume |
98	| Mute button (HUD) | All | Toggle audio |
99	
100	- Single jump (no double-jump in MVP). Jump arc is fixed height/duration, tuned so a well-timed tap clears one obstacle.
101	- Jump is **edge-triggered** (fires on press, not hold) and ignored while airborne.
102	
103	> Duck/slide is explicitly **deferred to phase 2** (§9). Spec'd here as absent so level design assumes a jump-only vocabulary.
104	
105	### 3.3 Entities
106	
107	| Entity | Role | Behavior |
108	|---|---|---|
109	| **Hero dog** | Player avatar | Auto-runs; fixed screen X; jumps on input; has HP |
110	| **Tick** | Damaging obstacle / enemy | Ground or low-flying hazard; collision = **−1 HP**. The thing you must avoid |
111	| **Environmental obstacle** (bush / puddle) | Jump obstacle | Per brief §3A; collision = **−1 HP** (treated as a hazard you jump). *Assumption: same damage model as tick; confirm if bush/puddle should be harmless-but-blocking instead* (§11) |
112	| **Tablet** | Collectible (the product) | Pickup = **+score** and **+1 HP** up to the 3-heart cap |
113	| **Armor / shield pickup** | Timed power-up | Pickup = temporary invulnerability (see §3.7) |
114	| **Finish line** | Level end | Reaching it = Victory |
115	
116	> **Note on tick damage.** The brief (§2) describes ticks as "remove health / **deduct points**." This spec **intentionally replaces the points-deduction reading with HP-only damage** (−1 HP, no score penalty): it's simpler to communicate, and avoids negative-score confusion for a casual mobile audience. Score only ever goes up (§3.5).
117	
118	### 3.4 Health rules (locked)
119	
120	- Player starts with **3 HP**, shown as 3 hearts.
121	- **Tick collision: −1 HP.** Environmental-obstacle collision: −1 HP (see assumption above).
122	- **Tablet pickup: +1 HP**, capped at 3 (never exceeds the 3-heart max).
123	- **0 HP → Game Over.**
124	- On taking damage: brief invulnerability/blink window (~1 s) + hit animation, so a single obstacle can't drain multiple hearts in one contact.
125	
126	### 3.5 Scoring (locked direction)
127	
128	- **Tablets collected → +score** (primary source; ties score to the product).
129	- **Distance / survival → +score** over time (secondary, keeps score moving).
130	- Score is displayed live in the HUD and reported in `finish_game` (§7).
131	- **Combo / score-multiplier is deferred to phase 2** (§9). MVP score is a straight sum.
132	
133	*Exact point values (e.g. tablet = 100, per-second = 10) are tuning parameters, set during playtest.*
134	
135	### 3.6 Win / lose conditions (locked)
136	
137	| Outcome | Trigger | Result screen | Analytics |
138	|---|---|---|---|
139	| **Victory** | Reach the finish line with ≥1 HP | Victory screen | `finish_game` `result:'win'` |
140	| **Game Over** | HP reaches 0 before finish | Game Over screen | `finish_game` `result:'lose'` |
141	
142	Both screens surface the same buy CTA (§6.4).
143	
144	### 3.7 Armor power-up (locked — optional feature IN MVP)
145	
146	Per brief §3 ("medication as Armor", Crash-Bandicoot-mask principle):
147	
148	- A distinct **Armor/shield pickup** appears occasionally in the level.
149	- On pickup: hero gains **temporary total invulnerability** — tick/obstacle collisions do **no damage** for the duration.
150	- **Distinct visual:** a shield aura / mask-style overlay on the dog (brief's Crash-Bandicoot mask reference), plus a countdown/expiry tell (aura flashes as it runs out).
151	- Duration is a tuning parameter (proposed **~4–6 s**).
152	- While armored, hitting a tick still consumes/destroys the tick (feels powerful) but costs no HP.
153	- Reinforces the marketing message: *the tablet is the protection.*
154	
155	### 3.8 Difficulty progression (locked)
156	
157	The level ramps over its ~60–90 s so the finish feels earned:
158	
159	- **Scroll speed** increases in stages from start to finish.
160	- **Obstacle & tick density** increases (tighter spacing, more frequent hazards).
161	- **Tablet/armor generosity** tapers slightly late-game to raise tension near the finish.
162	- Ramp is authored/curve-driven (not purely random) so difficulty is repeatable and tunable. Spacing always stays clearable with jump-only controls (§3.2).
163	
164	### 3.9 Session length & level termination (locked)
165	
166	**One finite level, ~60–90 s.** Not endless. This keeps sessions short, guarantees most players reach a result screen (and thus the CTA), and bounds art/level-authoring scope.
167	
168	**Level length is distance-based.** The level is a fixed **world distance** measured in world units — `LEVEL_LENGTH` (a `gameConfig` tuning value) — sized so that traversing it at the base scroll speed takes the target **~60–90 s**. (Because the difficulty ramp *increases* speed over the run (§3.8), the actual traversal time is somewhat under the base-speed figure; `LEVEL_LENGTH` is tuned against the full speed curve during playtest to land in the 60–90 s window.) Player progress is tracked as distance travelled toward `LEVEL_LENGTH`, and the HUD progress bar (§6.2) maps to `distance / LEVEL_LENGTH`.
169	
170	**Finish-line spawn rule:** a **FinishLine** entity is spawned once, at world position `LEVEL_LENGTH` (the end of the level distance). No further obstacles/ticks spawn past it. When the hero reaches/overlaps the FinishLine with ≥1 HP, the run ends in **Victory** (§3.6).
171

324	## 7. Analytics & Tracking Spec

326	### 7.1 Adapter design

329	
330	```ts
331	type AnalyticsEvent = 'start_game' | 'finish_game' | 'click_buy';
332	
333	function track(event: AnalyticsEvent, params: Record<string, unknown> = {}): void {
334	  // GA4
335	  window.gtag?.('event', event, params);
336	  // Meta Pixel — custom events via trackCustom
337	  window.fbq?.('trackCustom', event, params);
338	  // Dev/QA: console mirror when a debug flag is on
339	  if (DEBUG_ANALYTICS) console.debug('[track]', event, params);
340	}
341	```
342	
343	Rationale:
344	- **One contract, two sinks.** Adding/removing a sink (or a consent gate) is a one-file change.
345	- **Safe if a pixel is absent.** Optional chaining means a missing/blocked `gtag`/`fbq` never throws (ad-blockers are common on the audience).
346	- **Testable.** Event emission can be asserted in isolation.

348	### 7.2 Event / parameter contract
349	
350	#### `start_game` — a round begins
351	
352	| Param | Type | Required | Example | Notes |
353	|---|---|---|---|---|
354	| *(none required)* | — | — | — | Fired once when the Play scene starts the run |

357

492	## 10. Non-Functional Requirements
493	
494	### 10.1 Performance
495	
496	- Meet the budget in §2.3 (confirm targets). 60 FPS mid-range, ≥30 FPS floor low-end.
497	- Object pooling for spawned entities (ticks, tablets, obstacles) — no per-spawn GC churn.
498	- Atlas-based rendering to minimize draw calls.
499	
500	### 10.2 iOS Safari audio-unlock (locked requirement)
501	
502	- Web audio on iOS Safari is **suspended until a user gesture**. The AudioManager must **resume the audio context on the first tap** (Play button / first canvas tap) before playing music/SFX.
503	- Phaser's audio unlock helps, but we verify explicitly on iOS: no audio before first gesture, correct audio after.
504	- Mute state must survive the unlock (a muted player who taps Play stays muted).
505	
506	### 10.3 Browser support
507	
508	- Meet the matrix in §2.2. Primary QA on iOS Safari + Android Chrome.
509	- Graceful handling of blocked analytics (ad-blockers) — game fully playable with `gtag`/`fbq` absent (§7.1).
510	
511	### 10.4 Accessibility (basic, appropriate to an advergame)
512	
513	- Large, thumb-friendly tap targets; the whole canvas is the jump zone.
514	- Sufficient text/HUD contrast; hearts distinguishable by shape+fill, not color alone.
515	- Mute control always reachable.
516	- Full keyboard play on desktop (spacebar jump).
517	- No essential info conveyed by color alone.
518	- *(Full WCAG conformance is out of scope for a game canvas; this is a reasonable-effort baseline.)*
519	
520	### 10.5 Asset-size mindfulness
521	
522	- Stay within the download budget (§2.3): pack atlases tightly, compress audio, avoid oversized backgrounds (scale parallax art to max device resolution, not beyond).
523	- Lazy-load nothing critical to first play; everything needed for round 1 loads in Preload behind the bar.
524	- Prefer tint/shader variants over duplicate sheets (e.g. armored dog) to save bytes.

1	# Game Specification — 2D Browser Runner (Working title: *Happy Dog Runner*)
2	
3	**Document type:** Product & technical specification (buildable scope for estimate)
4	**Status:** Draft for client confirmation
5	**Source of requirements:** [`docs/2d-browser-runner-bi-brief.md`](./2d-browser-runner-bi-brief.md) (client cost-estimation brief, English translation)
6	**Date:** 2026-07-23
7	
8	> **How to read this document.** The client brief is the source of *requirements*. A product interview then locked a set of *decisions* that resolve the brief's open ambiguities (e.g. endless vs. finite, MVP vs. phase 2). Where a locked decision narrows or overrides the brief, this spec follows the decision and says so. Section 11 lists what still needs client confirmation before a firm cost/timeline can be committed.
9	
10	---
11	
12	## 1. Overview & Goals
13	
14	### 1.1 What we are building
15	
16	A **mobile-first, branded 2D browser runner** that promotes a dog flea-and-tick tablet. The player controls a hero dog that auto-runs through a park, jumps over obstacles, avoids **ticks**, and collects **tablets**. The round is a **finite single level (~60–90 s)** ending in **Victory** (reach the finish line) or **Game Over** (lose all health). After the round, a single call-to-action surfaces a **promo code** and links to **[tabletki.ua](http://tabletki.ua)** to buy the product.
17	
18	This is an advergame: the gameplay is the vehicle, and the marketing outcomes are the point.
19	
20	### 1.2 Marketing objective
21	
22	Per the brief (§1), two goals:
23	
24	1. **Awareness** — teach, through play, that ticks are a threat and the tablet is the protection. The "tablet as armor" power-up (§3.7) makes the product mechanic *be* the protection.
25	2. **Conversion** — drive tablet purchase via the post-round CTA to tabletki.ua (brief §3, "CTA button").
26	
27	### 1.3 Audience
28	
29	Dog owners on **mobile web**, reached through paid social / display where Meta Pixel and GA4 attribution matter. Casual players; sessions are short and one-handed. UI language assumed **Ukrainian primary**, built i18n-ready (see §11).
30	
31	### 1.4 Success signals (tied to the three analytics events)
32	
33	The entire funnel is observable through three events (full contract in §7):
34	
35	| Funnel stage | Signal | Event |
36	|---|---|---|
37	| Engagement | Player starts a round | `start_game` |
38	| Completion & quality | Player finishes (win or lose), with score & duration | `finish_game` (`result`, `score`, `duration_s`) |
39	| **Conversion** | Player taps the buy CTA | `click_buy` (`destination`, `promo_code`) |
40	
41	Primary KPI is `click_buy / start_game` (intent-to-purchase rate). `finish_game` with `result=win` vs. `lose` and `duration_s` tells us whether difficulty is tuned so players actually reach the CTA.
42	
43	---
44	
45	## 2. Platforms & Performance Targets
46	
47	### 2.1 Platform priority
48	
49	**Mobile web first**, desktop supported (brief §2). Touch is the primary input; desktop uses tap/click and spacebar.
50	
51	### 2.2 Supported browser matrix
52	
53	| Tier | Browser / OS | Support level |
54	|---|---|---|
55	| Primary | iOS Safari (last 2 major versions) | Fully supported, primary QA target |
56	| Primary | Android Chrome (last 2 major versions) | Fully supported, primary QA target |
57	| Secondary | Desktop Chrome / Edge / Firefox (current) | Fully supported |
58	| Secondary | Desktop Safari (current) | Fully supported |
59	| Best-effort | Samsung Internet, mobile Firefox | Should work; not a QA gate |
60	
61	### 2.3 Performance budget (assumed — **flag for confirmation**, see §11)
62	
63	Because the brief sets no numbers, we propose these targets. They drive art budgets and QA gates and must be confirmed:
64	
65	| Metric | Target | Notes |
66	|---|---|---|
67	| Frame rate | 60 FPS on mid-range phones; **≥30 FPS floor** on low-end (≈2–3-year-old Android) | Gameplay must never dip below the floor |
68	| Time-to-interactive (first load, warm CDN) | **≤3 s** on a 4G connection | Menu interactive |
69	| Initial download (gzipped) | **≤4–6 MB** total (code + assets) | Aggressive for an advergame; see §10.5 |
70	| Input latency (tap → jump) | ≤1 frame of processing | Tap responsiveness is the whole game |
71	| Orientation | Portrait-first; graceful landscape | Confirm preferred orientation |
72	
73	These are the recommended KPIs to lock in §11.
74	
75	---
76	
77	## 3. Gameplay Design
78	
79	### 3.1 Core loop
80	
81	```
82	auto-run forward  →  read upcoming hazard  →  tap to jump  →  land / collect / take hit
83	      ↑                                                                    │
84	      └──────────────────── repeat until finish line or 0 HP ──────────────┘
85	```
86	
87	The player does exactly one thing — **time jumps** — against a scrolling stream of obstacles, ticks, and tablets. Skill = timing and reading density as speed ramps.
88	
89	### 3.2 Controls (locked)
90	
91	**Auto-run + tap-to-jump ONLY.** No duck/slide, no lane-switching in MVP.
92	
93	| Input | Platform | Action |
94	|---|---|---|
95	| Tap anywhere on canvas | Mobile | Jump |
96	| Spacebar / click | Desktop | Jump |
97	| Pause button (HUD) | All | Pause / resume |
98	| Mute button (HUD) | All | Toggle audio |
99	
100	- Single jump (no double-jump in MVP). Jump arc is fixed height/duration, tuned so a well-timed tap clears one obstacle.
101	- Jump is **edge-triggered** (fires on press, not hold) and ignored while airborne.
102	
103	> Duck/slide is explicitly **deferred to phase 2** (§9). Spec'd here as absent so level design assumes a jump-only vocabulary.
104	
105	### 3.3 Entities
106	
107	| Entity | Role | Behavior |
108	|---|---|---|
109	| **Hero dog** | Player avatar | Auto-runs; fixed screen X; jumps on input; has HP |
110	| **Tick** | Damaging obstacle / enemy | Ground or low-flying hazard; collision = **−1 HP**. The thing you must avoid |
111	| **Environmental obstacle** (bush / puddle) | Jump obstacle | Per brief §3A; collision = **−1 HP** (treated as a hazard you jump). *Assumption: same damage model as tick; confirm if bush/puddle should be harmless-but-blocking instead* (§11) |
112	| **Tablet** | Collectible (the product) | Pickup = **+score** and **+1 HP** up to the 3-heart cap |
113	| **Armor / shield pickup** | Timed power-up | Pickup = temporary invulnerability (see §3.7) |
114	| **Finish line** | Level end | Reaching it = Victory |
115	
116	> **Note on tick damage.** The brief (§2) describes ticks as "remove health / **deduct points**." This spec **intentionally replaces the points-deduction reading with HP-only damage** (−1 HP, no score penalty): it's simpler to communicate, and avoids negative-score confusion for a casual mobile audience. Score only ever goes up (§3.5).
117	
118	### 3.4 Health rules (locked)
119	
120	- Player starts with **3 HP**, shown as 3 hearts.
121	- **Tick collision: −1 HP.** Environmental-obstacle collision: −1 HP (see assumption above).
122	- **Tablet pickup: +1 HP**, capped at 3 (never exceeds the 3-heart max).
123	- **0 HP → Game Over.**
124	- On taking damage: brief invulnerability/blink window (~1 s) + hit animation, so a single obstacle can't drain multiple hearts in one contact.
125	
126	### 3.5 Scoring (locked direction)
127	
128	- **Tablets collected → +score** (primary source; ties score to the product).
129	- **Distance / survival → +score** over time (secondary, keeps score moving).
130	- Score is displayed live in the HUD and reported in `finish_game` (§7).
131	- **Combo / score-multiplier is deferred to phase 2** (§9). MVP score is a straight sum.
132	
133	*Exact point values (e.g. tablet = 100, per-second = 10) are tuning parameters, set during playtest.*
134	
135	### 3.6 Win / lose conditions (locked)
136	
137	| Outcome | Trigger | Result screen | Analytics |
138	|---|---|---|---|
139	| **Victory** | Reach the finish line with ≥1 HP | Victory screen | `finish_game` `result:'win'` |
140	| **Game Over** | HP reaches 0 before finish | Game Over screen | `finish_game` `result:'lose'` |
141	
142	Both screens surface the same buy CTA (§6.4).
143	
144	### 3.7 Armor power-up (locked — optional feature IN MVP)
145	
146	Per brief §3 ("medication as Armor", Crash-Bandicoot-mask principle):
147	
148	- A distinct **Armor/shield pickup** appears occasionally in the level.
149	- On pickup: hero gains **temporary total invulnerability** — tick/obstacle collisions do **no damage** for the duration.
150	- **Distinct visual:** a shield aura / mask-style overlay on the dog (brief's Crash-Bandicoot mask reference), plus a countdown/expiry tell (aura flashes as it runs out).
151	- Duration is a tuning parameter (proposed **~4–6 s**).
152	- While armored, hitting a tick still consumes/destroys the tick (feels powerful) but costs no HP.
153	- Reinforces the marketing message: *the tablet is the protection.*
154	
155	### 3.8 Difficulty progression (locked)
156	
157	The level ramps over its ~60–90 s so the finish feels earned:
158	
159	- **Scroll speed** increases in stages from start to finish.
160	- **Obstacle & tick density** increases (tighter spacing, more frequent hazards).
161	- **Tablet/armor generosity** tapers slightly late-game to raise tension near the finish.
162	- Ramp is authored/curve-driven (not purely random) so difficulty is repeatable and tunable. Spacing always stays clearable with jump-only controls (§3.2).
163	
164	### 3.9 Session length & level termination (locked)
165	
166	**One finite level, ~60–90 s.** Not endless. This keeps sessions short, guarantees most players reach a result screen (and thus the CTA), and bounds art/level-authoring scope.
167	
168	**Level length is distance-based.** The level is a fixed **world distance** measured in world units — `LEVEL_LENGTH` (a `gameConfig` tuning value) — sized so that traversing it at the base scroll speed takes the target **~60–90 s**. (Because the difficulty ramp *increases* speed over the run (§3.8), the actual traversal time is somewhat under the base-speed figure; `LEVEL_LENGTH` is tuned against the full speed curve during playtest to land in the 60–90 s window.) Player progress is tracked as distance travelled toward `LEVEL_LENGTH`, and the HUD progress bar (§6.2) maps to `distance / LEVEL_LENGTH`.
169

323	
324	## 7. Analytics & Tracking Spec
325	
326	### 7.1 Adapter design
327	
328	A **thin `track(event, params)` adapter** is the single choke point for all analytics. Game code never calls `gtag`/`fbq` directly — it calls `track()`, which fans out to **GA4 (gtag)** and **Meta Pixel (fbq)**.
329	
330	```ts
331	type AnalyticsEvent = 'start_game' | 'finish_game' | 'click_buy';
332	
333	function track(event: AnalyticsEvent, params: Record<string, unknown> = {}): void {
334	  // GA4
335	  window.gtag?.('event', event, params);
336	  // Meta Pixel — custom events via trackCustom
337	  window.fbq?.('trackCustom', event, params);
338	  // Dev/QA: console mirror when a debug flag is on
339	  if (DEBUG_ANALYTICS) console.debug('[track]', event, params);
340	}
341	```
342	
343	Rationale:
344	- **One contract, two sinks.** Adding/removing a sink (or a consent gate) is a one-file change.
345	- **Safe if a pixel is absent.** Optional chaining means a missing/blocked `gtag`/`fbq` never throws (ad-blockers are common on the audience).
346	- **Testable.** Event emission can be asserted in isolation.
347	
348	### 7.2 Event / parameter contract
349	
350	#### `start_game` — a round begins
351	
352	| Param | Type | Required | Example | Notes |
353	|---|---|---|---|---|
354	| *(none required)* | — | — | — | Fired once when the Play scene starts the run |
355	
356	#### `finish_game` — fires on BOTH Victory and Game Over
357	
358	| Param | Type | Required | Example | Notes |
359	|---|---|---|---|---|
360	| `result` | `'win' \| 'lose'` | ✅ | `'win'` | `win` = reached finish; `lose` = 0 HP |
361	| `score` | integer | ✅ | `1450` | Final score at round end |
362	| `duration_s` | integer (seconds) | ✅ | `72` | **Active play time, excluding paused time.** Measured by accumulating elapsed time each frame while the run is playing; the accumulator is **frozen while paused** (§6.3) so paused time never inflates it. Reported at round end |
363	
364	#### `click_buy` — CTA tapped on results screen
365	
366	| Param | Type | Required | Example | Notes |
367	|---|---|---|---|---|
368	| `destination` | string | ✅ | `'tabletki.ua'` | Fixed for MVP |
369	| `promo_code` | string | ✅ | `'DOG10'` | The code shown on the CTA (see §11) |
370	
371	> All three event **names** are fixed by the brief (§3B: `start_game`, `finish_game`, `click_buy`) — do not rename.
372	
373	### 7.3 GA4 (gtag) + Meta Pixel (fbq) wiring
374	
375	- Both snippets load in `index.html` `<head>` (standard install), parameterized by **GA4 Measurement ID** and **Meta Pixel ID** (see §11 — needed before launch).
376	- IDs injected via Vite env vars (`VITE_GA4_ID`, `VITE_FB_PIXEL_ID`) so staging/prod differ without code edits.
377	- GA4 receives events via `gtag('event', …)`; Meta Pixel via `fbq('trackCustom', …)`. (Meta standard events like `Purchase` are **not** used — the brief's three custom names take priority; a `Purchase` mapping can be added later if the client wants Ads Manager optimization on it.)
378	- **GA4 custom dimensions/metrics:** the custom params (`result`, `score`, `duration_s`, `destination`, `promo_code`) must be **registered as custom dimensions/metrics in the GA4 property** (GA4 Admin → Custom definitions) or they will be collected but **won't surface in GA4 reports**. Register `result`/`destination`/`promo_code` as dimensions and `score`/`duration_s` as metrics as part of launch setup.

380	### 7.4 Consent / GDPR note
381	
382	- The audience is EU-adjacent (Ukraine); ad pixels imply personal-data processing.
383	- **Recommendation:** a lightweight consent gate. `track()` is the natural enforcement point — buffer or drop events until consent is granted, and only initialize `fbq`/`gtag` post-consent (Consent Mode v2 for GA4).
384	- Exact consent UX / whether a CMP is required depends on the client's legal stance — **flag in §11.** MVP ships the adapter consent-ready even if the banner is deferred.

388	## 8. Technical Architecture
389	
390	### 8.1 Stack (locked)
391	
392	**Phaser 3 + TypeScript + Vite**, shipped as a **100% static site** (Cloudflare Pages or Netlify). **No backend/server.** (Brief §3B leaves engine to us and asks for "something simple"; Phaser 3 is the standard, well-supported HTML5 2D choice.)
393	
394	**Engine configuration:**
395	- **Physics:** Phaser **Arcade Physics** — the lightweight AABB engine, sufficient for a jump-and-collide runner and the cheapest option for the low-end-phone perf floor (§2.3). No need for Matter.js.
396	- **Scale mode:** `Phaser.Scale.FIT` with `autoCenter: Phaser.Scale.CENTER_BOTH` — the game renders at a fixed logical resolution and scales to fit any viewport while centered, which is the mobile-friendly default for the portrait-first target (§2.3) across the device matrix (§2.2).

399	
400	```

403	├─ vite.config.ts

483	|---|---|---|

492	## 10. Non-Functional Requirements
493	
494	### 10.1 Performance
495	
496	- Meet the budget in §2.3 (confirm targets). 60 FPS mid-range, ≥30 FPS floor low-end.
497	- Object pooling for spawned entities (ticks, tablets, obstacles) — no per-spawn GC churn.
498	- Atlas-based rendering to minimize draw calls.
499	
500	### 10.2 iOS Safari audio-unlock (locked requirement)
501	
502	- Web audio on iOS Safari is **suspended until a user gesture**. The AudioManager must **resume the audio context on the first tap** (Play button / first canvas tap) before playing music/SFX.
503	- Phaser's audio unlock helps, but we verify explicitly on iOS: no audio before first gesture, correct audio after.
504	- Mute state must survive the unlock (a muted player who taps Play stays muted).
505	
506	### 10.3 Browser support
507	
508	- Meet the matrix in §2.2. Primary QA on iOS Safari + Android Chrome.
509	- Graceful handling of blocked analytics (ad-blockers) — game fully playable with `gtag`/`fbq` absent (§7.1).
510	
511	### 10.4 Accessibility (basic, appropriate to an advergame)
512	
513	- Large, thumb-friendly tap targets; the whole canvas is the jump zone.
514	- Sufficient text/HUD contrast; hearts distinguishable by shape+fill, not color alone.
515	- Mute control always reachable.
516	- Full keyboard play on desktop (spacebar jump).
517	- No essential info conveyed by color alone.
518	- *(Full WCAG conformance is out of scope for a game canvas; this is a reasonable-effort baseline.)*
519	
520	### 10.5 Asset-size mindfulness
521	
522	- Stay within the download budget (§2.3): pack atlases tightly, compress audio, avoid oversized backgrounds (scale parallax art to max device resolution, not beyond).
523	- Lazy-load nothing critical to first play; everything needed for round 1 loads in Preload behind the bar.
524	- Prefer tint/shader variants over duplicate sheets (e.g. armored dog) to save bytes.

542	| 9 | **Orientation** (portrait vs landscape) & **CTA nav** (same/new tab on mobile) | Portrait-first; confirm CTA tab behavior |
543	| 10 | **Bush/puddle damage model** — damaging hazard vs harmless blocker | Treated as −1 HP hazard (§3.3) |

548	## 12. Estimate Framing

554	**MVP:**

559	- Scoring (tablets + survival).

561	- Entities: tick, tablet, bush/puddle, armor pickup (timed invulnerability logic).
562	- HUD (score, hearts, progress, pause, mute) + pause overlay.

564	- AudioManager (SFX, music loop, mute persistence, **iOS audio-unlock**).
565	- `track()` analytics adapter → GA4 + Meta Pixel; the 3-event contract (§7).
566	- Object pooling / performance pass; browser-matrix QA.

Read-only scout report for Happy Dog Runner. All cites are `file:line`. **Key headline finding: `AudioManager` is a mute/unlock/persistence shell only — it owns no sound keys and has no `play()`; audio assets are NOT in the manifest (it's SVG-only); and the pause system + pause button do not exist yet and must be built.**

## 1. SPEC_REQUIREMENTS

### HUD elements (spec §6.2, `docs/2d-browser-runner-spec.md:284-296`)
Persistent, minimal, thumb-safe. Proposed positions:

| Element | Position | Content |
|---|---|---|
| **Score** | Top-left | Live numeric (`hud_score` + number) |
| **HP hearts** | Top-center or top-left under score | 3 hearts, filled/empty — distinguishable by **shape+fill, not color alone** (§10.4, art-direction.md:60) |
| **Level progress** | Top, full-width thin bar | `distance / LEVEL_LENGTH`; **progress bar preferred over timer** (visualizes finish approaching) |
| **Pause** | Top-right | Opens pause overlay |
| **Mute** | Top-right (next to pause) | Toggles audio |

The HUD progress-bar art (`ui_progress_bar`) is **frame/track only — inner fill is transparent; code draws the dynamic fill on top** (art-direction.md:58).

### Pause & mute (spec §6.3, `:299-301`)
- **Pause overlay:** dims play; shows **Resume + Mute + (optional) Quit-to-menu**; **game clock AND scrolling freeze.**
- **Mute:** toggles all audio; state **persisted** (localStorage) across scenes/sessions; reflected by icon in **menu, HUD, and pause.**
- **`duration_s` must EXCLUDE paused time** (spec §7.2, `track.ts:33`) — currently `elapsedMs += delta` runs every frame (`GameScene.ts:278`), so pause MUST freeze that accumulation.

### Results screens (spec §6.4, `:303-321`)
Both share a layout; only framing/art differ:

| Element | Victory | Game Over |
|---|---|---|
| Headline | "Ти впорався! 🐕" | "Кліщі тебе наздогнали…" |
| Final score | shown | shown |
| Result art | `dog_victory` | `dog_defeat` |
| **Buy CTA (single)** | promo code + "Купити на tabletki.ua" | same |
| Secondary | Play again | Play again |

CTA (locked): **one** primary CTA → displays copyable **promo code** + button to **tabletki.ua**; on tap fire `click_buy` (`destination`, `promo_code`) **then** navigate to the **UTM-tagged** URL (new tab). **No client-site path in MVP** — tabletki.ua only.

### A11y basics (spec §10.4, `:511-518`)
- Large thumb-friendly tap targets; whole canvas = jump zone.
- Sufficient text/HUD contrast; hearts distinguishable by shape+fill not color alone.
- Mute always reachable.
- Full keyboard play on desktop (spacebar jump).
- No essential info by color alone.

### Analytics fire points — checklist (spec §5.2, `:262-270`; §7.2 `:349-371`)
- [x] **`start_game`** — fires once as Play/run begins. **ALREADY WIRED** in `GameScene.ts:121` (`track('start_game')`). No params.
- [x] **`finish_game`** `{result, score, duration_s}` — Victory/GameOver. **ALREADY WIRED** in `GameScene.ts:429` (`endRun`). Win at finish-line overlap (`:231`, `:294-296`); lose at HP≤0 (`:395`).
- [x] **`click_buy`** `{destination, promo_code}` — results CTA tap. **ALREADY WIRED** in `ResultsScene.ts:89` (`onBuy`), then `window.open(buildBuyUrl(), '_blank')` (`:90`).
- ⚠️ The only **new** analytics concern for Phase 4: ensuring `duration_s` excludes paused time once pause exists (§7.2 + `track.ts:33`). All three events and their param shapes are already implemented in `src/analytics/track.ts` (typed overloads `:57-59`; `FinishGameParams` `:29-34`).

### Screen flow (spec §5.1, `:245-259`)
`Menu → Play` (fires start_game) → `Victory|GameOver` (fires finish_game) → `Buy` (fires click_buy) or `Play again` (→ fresh start_game). Pause/Resume loops within Play. All scene keys exist (`src/scenes/keys.ts:2-8`): Boot/Preload/Menu/Game/Results.

## 2. AUDIOMANAGER_API

`AudioManager` (`src/systems/AudioManager.ts`) is an **object literal, not a class** — a thin wrapper over the scene's Phaser `BaseSoundManager`. **Full public API (all 4 methods):**

```ts
isMuted(): boolean                                              // AudioManager.ts:31-33
apply(sound: Phaser.Sound.BaseSoundManager): void               // :36-38 — pushes persisted mute: sound.mute = muted
toggle(sound: Phaser.Sound.BaseSoundManager): boolean           // :41-46 — flip + sound.mute + persist; returns new muted
installAudioUnlock(sound: Phaser.Sound.BaseSoundManager): void  // :60-78 — long-lived window pointerdown/touchend → context.resume() once
```

Internals worth knowing:
- Module-level state: `muted` (`:27`, seeded from localStorage `MUTE_STORAGE_KEY='hdr:muted'`, `gameConfig.ts:66`) and `unlockInstalled` guard (`:28`).
- `readStoredMute()`/`persistMute()` wrap localStorage in try/catch so private mode fails open (`:11-25`).

### Verdict: PRELOADED audio keys (not runtime buffers)
- It is built around **Phaser preloaded keys** — playback goes through the scene's `sound` manager (`this.sound.play(key)`), and mute is enforced by setting `sound.mute`. It expects sounds to have been registered via `Phaser.load.audio(...)` in a scene's `preload`.
- It does **NOT** own/register/track any sound keys, has **no `play()` / `add()` / key map**, and stores **no volume config**.
- It does **NOT** synthesize runtime Web Audio buffers/oscillators. **However**, it already reaches the underlying `WebAudioSoundManager.context` (`AudioManager.ts:66-69`) to resume it — so a synthesized-tone path is *physically reachable* via `sound.context`, but that is not the intended design. The clean, idiomatic path is **preloaded keys + `this.sound.play(key, { volume })`**.
- **How to play a sound (recommended):** directly `this.sound.play('sfx_jump')` (Phaser honors the `sound.mute` flag the AudioManager already syncs). Optionally add a tiny `AudioManager.play(sound, key, opts)` helper later, but it is not required — every sound manager already respects the shared mute.
- **iOS unlock requirement (spec §10.2):** handled — call already lives in BootScene. The only open item is the AudioManager's own `TODO(phase-5)` (`AudioManager.ts:58`): verify on real iOS Safari that a muted player who taps Play stays muted through unlock (mute is module state, unaffected by resume, so it should hold).

### ⚠️ Audio assets are NOT loadable today — seam to flag
- `ASSET_MANIFEST` (`assetManifest.ts:41-87`) is **SVG-only**; `AssetDef.type` is the literal `'svg'` (`assetManifest.ts:19`), and `PreloadScene.preload()` loops `load.svg` for every entry (`PreloadScene.ts:29-31`). There is **no audio loading anywhere** (grep for `load.audio` returns nothing).
- **You cannot simply append audio to the existing manifest** without widening `AssetDef.type` and the `gen-placeholders` contract. Recommendation: add a **separate audio key map** (e.g. a small `AUDIO_KEYS` set) + dedicated `this.load.audio(key, [url])` calls in `PreloadScene.preload()` (after the SVG loop). Per spec §8.4, use compressed `.m4a`/`.mp3` + `.ogg` fallback. The 7 required assets (spec §4.6, `:226-235`): jump SFX, hit SFX, pickup SFX, victory sting, game-over sting, music loop, + mute state (code).

### Whole-canvas jump handler to GATE (`buildInput()`, `GameScene.ts:265-271`)
```ts
this.input.on(Phaser.Input.Events.POINTER_DOWN, () => this.hero.jump());   // :267
this.input.keyboard?.addKey(SPACE).on('down', () => this.hero.jump());     // :269-270
```
Spec §3.2/§10.4: the whole canvas is the jump zone. Two new constraints Phase 4 must enforce:

1. **Taps on pause/mute UI must NOT jump.** Phaser's scene-level `POINTER_DOWN` fires even when an interactive GameObject (button) also receives the event, so it does **not** auto-exclude buttons.
2. **Taps while paused must NOT jump** (and the loop is frozen anyway).

**Recommended gating approach** — replace the `:267` handler with a guarded one:
```ts
this.input.on(Phaser.Input.Events.POINTER_DOWN, (pointer: Phaser.Input.Pointer) => {
  if (this.paused) return;                                   // (2) ignore while paused
  const hit = this.input.hitTestPointer(pointer);            // interactive objs under pointer
  if (hit.length > 0) return;                                // (1) a HUD button (pause/mute) ate it
  this.hero.jump();
});
```
- `hitTestPointer` returns the interactive GameObjects under the pointer — if any pause/mute button has `setInteractive`, its hit-area is reported and the tap is treated as a UI tap, not a jump.
- **No need to re-check airborne/grounded:** `HeroDog.jump()` (`HeroDog.ts:110-111`) already self-guards — *"fires only when grounded & alive; ignored airborne."* (Landing returns to run, `HeroDog.ts:186-189`.)
- A `paused` flag does not yet exist (grep: no `this.scene.pause`/`physics.pause`/`isPaused` anywhere). See Pause note below.

### Pause — does not exist yet (separate from jump gating, but coupled)
Grep found **zero** pause usage in the codebase. Two viable patterns:
- **In-scene overlay + `paused` flag:** set `this.paused = true`; short-circuit `update()` at the top (`:275` currently `if (this.finished) return;` → add `|| this.paused`). This freezes scrolling, spawning, scoring, **and** the `elapsedMs += delta` at `:278` (which is what makes `duration_s` exclude paused time — spec §7.2). Render the `ui_pause_panel` + Resume/Mute/Quit as interactive GameObjects above the HUD. Pause/resume should also stop/resume the music loop.
- **Separate `PauseScene`:** `this.scene.pause(SceneKey.Game)` + `this.scene.launch(SceneKey.Pause)`; pause-by-scene also halts `update()` and thus `elapsedMs`. Requires adding a `Pause` key to `src/scenes/keys.ts:2-8`.

Either works; the in-scene flag is less machinery and keeps the `paused` guard the jump handler needs.
